findings.detail: GreenMet (Greentech Minerals Holdings Inc.) CEO Drew Horn (former Pence aide, national security official). Shareholders include George Sorial (Trump Org EVP 2002-2019) and Keith Schiller (Trump Org security director, ran Oval Office ops). Both resigned as board members/advisors early 2025 but remain passive minority shareholders. Former Chief Geologist Ned Mamula (ex-CIA analyst) became USGS Director (Oct 2025), recently divested. GreenMet partnered with Tanbreez Mining Greenland A/S (Apr 2025) for rare earth mining - described as 'only shovel ready rare earth project in Greenland'. Helped secure $120M EXIM letter of interest for Tanbreez. Critical Metals Corp took controlling interest in Tanbreez (Sep 2025).

findings.summary: GreenMet (Greentech Minerals Holdings Inc.) is a Delaware-incorporated company registered at 1825 K St NW Ste 515, DC 20006. SAM.gov: UEI ZD31U1MMR4J7, CAGE 9VEL9, incorporated 2021-04-09. Primary NAICS 551114. SAM POCs: Andrew Horn (CEO) and Nicholas Denno (Dir Ops). Two related DC-registered LLCs at same address (GreenMet Consulting LLC and GreenMet Real Asset Management LLC), both now withdrawn.

Three Trump-era officials are beneficial owners of GreenMet: George Sorial (Trump Org EVP/Chief Compliance Counsel 2002-2019), Keith Schiller (Trump bodyguard/Dir Oval Office Operations), and Drew Horn (aide to VP Pence, national security official, ex-Army Special Forces/USMC). Sorial and Schiller resigned board/advisory roles early 2025 but remain passive shareholders. Ned Mamula served as GreenMet Chief Geologist before being confirmed as USGS Director (Oct 2025); filed divestiture Jan 2026. In Dec 2024, Sorial and Schiller formed Javelin Advisors LLC, a government relations firm now registered as foreign agent for Pakistan on rare earth minerals deal.

GreenMet brokered partnership between Critical Metals Corp (NASDAQ: CRML) and Tanbreez Mining Greenland A/S for Greenland REE development. Critical Metals acquiring 42-92.5% of Tanbreez from Rimbal Pty Ltd (Gregory Barnes). EXIM Bank issued M LOI for 15-year term loan under Supply Chain Resiliency Initiative. Tanbreez PEA: NPV .04B, IRR 180%, 4.7B tonne deposit with 27% HREE content. GreenMet also facilitated 10-year offtake between Critical Metals and Ucore Rare Metals for up to 10K tonnes/year REE concentrates to Ucore DoD-funded Strategic Metals Complex in Louisiana.

Libra Group (CEO: George Logothetis) made strategic investment in GreenMet in March 2022. Four Libra Group executive team members appointed to GreenMet board. Libra Group is an international business group with subsidiaries in 50+ countries spanning energy, shipping, real estate, and hospitality. This investment provided GreenMet capital and board-level international business connections.

GreenMet lobbied continuously from Q2 2021 through 2023 on critical minerals policy, targeting DEF (defense), NAT (natural resources), and ENG (energy) issue areas. Lobbying focused on NDAA critical minerals provisions, rare earth policy development, and mining permitting. Critical Metals Corp also began lobbying in 2025 on critical minerals supply chain advocacy. GreenMet registered in SAM.gov (March 2024) for government contracting eligibility, purpose code Z2 (federal assistance).

GreenMet CEO Drew Horn is pursuing a 1.5-gigawatt AI data center in Greenland (Kangerlussuaq area), projected multi-billion dollar cost. Aims for 300MW by mid-2027, 1.5GW by end 2028. GreenMet claims binding investor commitments for half of initial and final phase. However, Greenland government told CNBC it has not engaged in dialogue with Horn or GreenMet about the project. No land or local approvals secured. This represents expansion beyond minerals into AI infrastructure.
McKeon Group lobbied for both GreenMet and USA Rare Earth -- shared lobbying firm between two rare earth companies in investigation
findings.detail: The McKeon Group Inc., headed by former House Armed Services Committee Chairman Howard Buck McKeon, lobbied for GreenMet from Q4 2021 through Q3 2023 (total ~269500 income). McKeon Group also lobbied for USA Rare Earth (identified in LDA 2024 filings). This connects two rare earth/critical minerals companies in the investigation through a common defense-focused lobbying firm led by a former HASC chairman.

findings.summary: George Sorial and Keith Schiller appear in Washington DC corporate registry documents as beneficial owners of GreenMet (Greentech Minerals Holdings Inc.), alongside CEO Drew Horn. Sorial stated they are 'passive minority shareholders in GreenMet and have no management role in the company.' They resigned board/advisor roles in early 2025 but retained shares. Company HQ: 1825 K St NW 515 Washington DC 20006. Founded 2021.

GreenMet's compensation for brokering the Critical Metals Corp (CRML) / Tanbreez partnership is NOT disclosed in any CRML SEC filing (confirmed: 0 EDGAR results for GreenMet or Sorial). GreenMet's press release describes itself as facilitating the April 2025 strategic partnership and the August 2025 10-year offtake LOI between CRML/Tanbreez and Ucore Rare Metals for a DOD-funded Louisiana processing facility. GreenMet's role described as 'played a central role in facilitating the partnership, aligning commercial objectives, and ensuring strategic coordination.' No compensation terms disclosed.

GreenMet (fka Greentech Minerals Holdings Inc.) hired McKeon Group Inc as LDA registered lobbyist beginning Q4 2021 through at least Q1 2024. Lobbying issues: Natural Resources, Defense, Environment/Energy for 'rare earth and critical elements policy.' Government entities contacted include: DOD, White House Office, NSC, NEC, State Dept, Senate, House, Interior Dept, Energy Dept. Total disclosed lobbying income to McKeon: ,500 across 20 filings. Peak quarter Q2 2022: ,500. Lobbyist: Adam Raezler.

Greentech Minerals Holdings Inc. signed a Financing and Purchase Option Agreement with Texas Mineral Resources Corp. (TMRC) on November 8, 2021. Greentech agreed to fund a $6.5M bankable feasibility study for TMRC's Black Hawk Mining District silver project in NM in exchange for 20.2% equity in a proposed TMRC-Santa Fe Gold JV. The deal was abandoned when Greentech determined not to pursue the financing option per TMRC Q1 FY2023 10-Q.

GreenMet's compensation structure for the CRML-Tanbreez brokerage is structurally invisible. After reviewing all 167 CRML SEC filings (via EDGAR full-text search), the 2024 and 2025 20-F annual reports, and all 6-K press releases, GreenMet is mentioned in ZERO CRML SEC filings. GreenMet's own press releases describe its role as 'facilitating the partnership, aligning commercial objectives, and ensuring strategic coordination' but disclose no fees, equity compensation, advisory agreement, or financial arrangement. The compensation mechanism (if any) is not publicly disclosed.

GreenMet's three-division corporate structure maps to specific legal entities: (1) GreenMet Advisory = GreenMet Consulting LLC (DC Foreign LLC C00007696390, withdrawn). (2) GreenMet Capital = GreenMet Real Asset Management LLC (DC Foreign LLC C00007684320, withdrawn). (3) GreenMet Innovation = GreenMet Technologies LLC (entity not found in any ingested registries — DC, FL, NY, DE searches returned zero results; OpenCorporates unavailable due to API key). The absence of GreenMet Technologies LLC from public registries is investigatively significant.

GreenMet's lobbying expenditure: McKeon Group Inc. lobbied for GreenMet from Q4 2021 through Q3 2023, generating disclosed income of: Q4 2021 $12,000; Q1 2022 $30,000; Q2 2022 $77,500; Q3 2022 $30,000; Q4 2022 $30,000; Q1 2023 $30,000; Q2 2023 $40,000; Q3 2023 $20,000. Total McKeon Group paid by GreenMet: ~$269,500. From Q2 2023 onwards, GreenMet self-lobbied through in-house arm Greentech Minerals Holdings LLC (fka GreenMet Consulting), targeting DoD, DoE, DoS, OSTP, Commerce, DLA, NSC, EOP, Treasury, USTDA.

curation.lead:
GreenMet, formally Greentech Minerals Holdings Inc., is a Delaware-incorporated critical minerals advisory and brokerage firm founded in April 2021 and headquartered at 1825 K Street NW, Suite 515, Washington, DC [Finding #6164]. The company was founded by Drew Horn, a former Army Special Forces officer and aide to Vice President Mike Pence who later served in national security roles at the Department of Energy and ODNI [Finding #6166]. Its beneficial owners include George Sorial, the Trump Organization's Executive Vice President and Chief Compliance Counsel from 2002 to 2019, and Keith Schiller, Trump's longtime personal bodyguard and Director of Oval Office Operations, both of whom resigned board and advisory roles in early 2025 but remain passive minority shareholders [Finding #6331] [Finding #6166].

GreenMet operates at the intersection of critical minerals policy, government lobbying, and international deal brokerage. Its central accomplishment is facilitating the partnership between Critical Metals Corp (NASDAQ: CRML) and Tanbreez Mining Greenland A/S for what is described as the only shovel-ready rare earth project in Greenland, a deal that attracted a $120 million EXIM Bank letter of interest and a 10-year offtake agreement with Ucore Rare Metals for a DoD-funded processing facility in Louisiana [Finding #6168]. Analysis of SEC filings indicates that despite GreenMet's self-described "central role in facilitating the partnership, aligning commercial objectives, and ensuring strategic coordination," the company appears in zero of Critical Metals Corp's 167 SEC filings, and no compensation arrangement has been publicly disclosed [Finding #6368] [Finding #6332].

The company's significance extends beyond any single deal. Sorial and Schiller went on to co-found Javelin Advisors LLC in December 2024, a government relations firm that registered under FARA as a foreign agent for Pakistan on a rare earth minerals framework valued at up to $1 trillion [Finding #6166]. Meanwhile, Ned Mamula, GreenMet's former Chief Geologist, was confirmed as Director of the U.S. Geological Survey in October 2025 -- the federal agency that maintains the Critical Minerals List directly relevant to GreenMet's business [Finding #6154]. The personnel connections between GreenMet, Javelin Advisors, and federal agencies overseeing the critical minerals sector illustrate revolving-door dynamics within the Trump administration's Greenland and minerals policy.
curation.system_role: GreenMet is a critical minerals advisory and brokerage firm whose principals -- including former Trump Organization executives and national security officials -- rotate between private deal-making, government lobbying through the related firm Javelin Advisors, and federal positions overseeing the minerals sector. The company brokers rare earth partnerships across Greenland, Pakistan, and the domestic supply chain, with compensation arrangements that remain undisclosed in public filings.

sections.title: Corporate Identity and Structure
sections.content:
Greentech Minerals Holdings Inc. was incorporated in Delaware on April 9, 2021, and is registered in Washington, DC, at 1825 K Street NW, Suite 515 [Finding #6164]. The company is registered in SAM.gov under UEI ZD31U1MMR4J7 and CAGE code 9VEL9, with primary NAICS code 551114 (Corporate, Subsidiary, and Regional Managing Offices) and a purpose code of Z2 (federal assistance) [Finding #6164]. SAM.gov lists Andrew Horn (CEO) and Nicholas Denno (Director of Operations) as points of contact [Finding #6164].

Analysis of registry records indicates that GreenMet organized itself into three branded divisions, each mapped to a separate legal entity: GreenMet Advisory corresponded to GreenMet Consulting LLC (DC Foreign LLC C00007696390, now withdrawn); GreenMet Capital corresponded to GreenMet Real Asset Management LLC (DC Foreign LLC C00007684320, also withdrawn); and GreenMet Innovation was described as GreenMet Technologies LLC, which does not appear in any searched corporate registry across DC, Florida, New York, or Delaware [Finding #6372]. The withdrawal of the two registered subsidiaries and the absence of the third from public registries leaves unclear which corporate entities currently carry the company's operational activities.

sections.title: Key Personnel and Ownership Network
sections.content:
Washington, DC, corporate registry documents identify three beneficial owners of GreenMet: Drew Horn (CEO), George Sorial, and Keith Schiller [Finding #6331]. Horn is a former Army Special Forces and Marine Corps officer who served as an aide to Vice President Pence, a national security official at the Department of Energy, and a Senior Advisor at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence before founding GreenMet [Finding #6166]. Sorial served as the Trump Organization's Executive Vice President and Chief Compliance Counsel for approximately seventeen years (2002-2019), while Schiller was Donald Trump's personal bodyguard for decades before serving as Director of Oval Office Operations in the first Trump administration [Finding #6166]. Sorial has stated that he and Schiller are "passive minority shareholders in GreenMet and have no management role in the company," having resigned board and advisory roles in early 2025 [Finding #6331].

Ned Mamula served as GreenMet's Chief Geologist before being confirmed as Director of the U.S. Geological Survey in October 2025 [Finding #6154]. Mamula is a former CIA geoscientist whose career spanned USGS, DOE, CIA, and the Cato Institute [Finding #6154]. According to OCCRP reporting, Horn co-authored the foreword to Mamula's 2024 book Undermining Power [Finding #6154]. Mamula filed a divestiture from GreenMet in January 2026 following his confirmation, but the USGS directorship gives him authority over the Critical Minerals List -- a designation directly relevant to GreenMet's business interests [Finding #6154].

In March 2022, the Libra Group, an international business conglomerate led by CEO George Logothetis with subsidiaries spanning energy, shipping, real estate, and hospitality across 50-plus countries, made a strategic investment in GreenMet and placed four executive team members on the board [Finding #6169]. This investment provided GreenMet with capital and international business connections beyond its Washington policy network.

sections.title: Greenland Rare Earth Brokerage
sections.content:
GreenMet's principal deal-making centers on Greenland. In April 2025, GreenMet partnered with Tanbreez Mining Greenland A/S, which holds what it describes as the only shovel-ready rare earth project in Greenland, with a 4.7-billion-tonne deposit containing 27% heavy rare earth elements [Finding #6168]. GreenMet then brokered a partnership between Critical Metals Corp (NASDAQ: CRML) and Tanbreez, under which Critical Metals would acquire between 42% and 92.5% of Tanbreez from Rimbal Pty Ltd [Finding #6168]. By September 2025, Critical Metals had taken a controlling interest in Tanbreez [Finding #6154].

GreenMet also facilitated U.S. government financial backing for the deal. The EXIM Bank issued a $120 million letter of interest for a 15-year term loan under its Supply Chain Resiliency Initiative [Finding #6168]. Separately, GreenMet brokered a 10-year offtake agreement between Critical Metals and Ucore Rare Metals for up to 10,000 tonnes per year of rare earth concentrates to be processed at Ucore's DoD-funded Strategic Metals Complex in Louisiana [Finding #6168]. A preliminary economic assessment of the Tanbreez deposit projected a net present value of $3.04 billion and an internal rate of return of 180% [Finding #6168].

Analysis of SEC filings indicates that despite GreenMet's self-described "central role in facilitating the partnership, aligning commercial objectives, and ensuring strategic coordination," the company does not appear in any of Critical Metals Corp's 167 SEC filings [Finding #6368]. Analysis of EDGAR records shows a comprehensive search for "GreenMet," "Sorial," or "Schiller" in CRML filings returned zero results [Finding #6368]. Records indicate that no fees, equity compensation, advisory agreement, or other financial arrangement between GreenMet and Critical Metals has been publicly disclosed [Finding #6332]. Cantor Fitzgerald, led by Howard Lutnick (now U.S. Commerce Secretary), held shares in Critical Metals Corp as its SPAC underwriter, creating a further nexus between the administration and this supply chain [Finding #6168].

sections.title: The Javelin Advisors
sections.content:
In December 2024, GreenMet co-owners Sorial and Schiller, along with attorney Robert W. Seiden, formed Javelin Advisors LLC in Delaware, branding itself as "Founded by Insiders. Defined by Access" [Finding #6166]. On April 25, 2025, Javelin registered under FARA (Registration No. 7579) as a foreign agent for the Islamic Republic of Pakistan to pursue a rare earth minerals agreement with the United States [Finding #6166]. According to FARA filings, Pakistan paid Javelin $50,000 per month, routed through Seiden Law LLP as intermediary, generating $200,000 in documented payments before the FARA registration was terminated on October 8, 2025 [Finding #6166].

The Pakistan engagement produced material results. FARA filings reference a May 2025 framework for U.S.-Pakistan cooperation on rare earth minerals with an indicative value of up to $1 trillion, with Pakistan's Frontier Works Organisation (a military engineering corps) nominated as the extraction entity [Finding #6166]. Javelin used Rep. Ronny Jackson as its primary congressional contact, arranging an in-person meeting on May 1, 2025, between Jackson and Pakistani officials, followed by a series of calls that led to a draft memorandum of understanding delivered to the office of Rep. Ryan Zinke [Finding #6166]. The MoU ultimately resulted in a reported $30 million deal between US Strategic Metals and Pakistan's Frontier Works Organisation in September 2025 [Finding #6166].

According to public filings, Javelin's client roster extended well beyond minerals. In its first full year, the firm generated approximately $3.4 million across six clients: Logical Strategies LLC ($1.2 million for EPA asbestos regulation lobbying, owned by Giorgi Rtskhiladze), Fred Daibes ($1 million for executive clemency lobbying -- Daibes was convicted alongside Sen. Menendez), NioCorp Developments Ltd ($400,000 for critical minerals DoD contracts), Capstone USA Advisory Group ($300,000 for Ukraine reconstruction), Greg E. Lindberg (executive pardon), and I-MEI Foods Co. Ltd. of Taiwan (DoD food, cybersecurity, and robotics contracts) [Finding #6166]. Javelin concurrently operated foreign agent work for Pakistan, pardon brokering for convicted felons, and defense lobbying for critical minerals companies, all built on the same personnel network as GreenMet.

sections.title: Lobbying Strategy and Political Influence
sections.content:
Analysis of 37 LDA filings indicates that GreenMet's lobbying activity evolved through four phases: phase one (Q2-Q4 2021) used Strategies 360 with lobbyist Ami Sanchez at $10,000; phase two (Q4 2021-Q3 2023) engaged the McKeon Group Inc., headed by former House Armed Services Committee Chairman Howard "Buck" McKeon, generating approximately $269,500 in disclosed income [Finding #6373] [Finding #6338]; phase three (Q2 2023-Q2 2024) expanded to an in-house team of six lobbyists covering NDAA provisions, Defense Production Act, critical mineral appropriations, IRA magnet tax credits, and national lab R&D; and LDA records show phase four (Q3 2024-present) contracted to a sole lobbyist, Sabrina Katz, covering defense, energy, manufacturing, natural resources, and trade/tariff issues [Finding #6209].

GreenMet targeted a broad range of government entities: DoD, DoE, DoS, OSTP, Commerce, DLA, NSC, EOP, Treasury, and USTDA [Finding #6373]. Cogent Strategies overlapped during phase three, adding $20,000 [Finding #6170]. According to biographical records, the Cogent lobbyist assigned to GreenMet was Andrew Kauders, a former senior adviser to Senator Robert Menendez (later convicted of bribery), who came to Cogent via the Podesta Group [Finding #6207].

The McKeon Group also lobbied for USA Rare Earth, connecting two critical minerals companies in the investigation through a common defense-focused lobbying firm [Finding #6206]. According to congressional records and LDA filings, Nicole Rodgers, GreenMet's former Chief Government and External Affairs Officer (Q3 2023-Q2 2024), founded the Alliance for Mineral Security, a national coalition advocating for U.S. mineral independence, testified before Congress on critical minerals, and later joined Squire Patton Boggs [Finding #6208].

sections.title: Greenland Data Center Ambitions
sections.content:
GreenMet's Greenland ambitions extend beyond minerals into AI infrastructure. According to media reports, in January 2026, AmForge Corporation (CEO Dan Whaley) signed a letter of intent with Svend Hardenberg's Inuit Development Company ApS for a 1.5-gigawatt AI data center at Kangerlussuaq, Greenland, with GreenMet serving as matchmaker and ongoing advisor [Finding #6172]. The project envisions 300 megawatts by mid-2027 via LNG barges, scaling to 1.5 gigawatts by end of 2028 through hydroelectric power, plus a subsea cable connection [Finding #6172]. GreenMet claims binding investor commitments for half of both the initial and final phases [Finding #6172].

Horn described the division of labor: "He handles everything related to Greenland and Denmark, I handle everything related to the United States" [Finding #6172]. However, the Greenland government told CNBC that it has not engaged in dialogue with Horn or GreenMet about the project, and no land or local approvals have been secured [Finding #6172]. The data center project positions Horn as a node connecting Hardenberg (who also connects to Ronald Lauder) with American capital and government backing, replicating the GreenMet pattern of brokering between foreign resource holders and U.S. institutional interests [Finding #6172].

sections.title: Financial Opacity and Abandoned Ventures
sections.content:
GreenMet's revenue model remains opaque. Analysis of filings indicates the company brokered partnerships involving a $120 million EXIM letter of interest, a controlling interest acquisition in Tanbreez, and a 10-year offtake agreement, yet its compensation for these services is undisclosed in any public filing [Finding #6368] [Finding #6332]. Records indicate that EDGAR full-text searches confirm neither GreenMet, Sorial, nor Javelin Advisors appears in any CRML SEC filing [Finding #6368]. Whether GreenMet was compensated through advisory fees, equity stakes, success fees, or some other mechanism remains unknown.

An earlier venture also ended without public explanation. In November 2021, GreenMet signed a Financing and Purchase Option Agreement with Texas Mineral Resources Corp. (TMRC), agreeing to fund a $6.5 million bankable feasibility study for TMRC's Black Hawk Mining District silver project in New Mexico in exchange for 20.2% equity in a proposed TMRC-Santa Fe Gold joint venture [Finding #6367]. GreenMet subsequently "determined not to pursue the financing option" per TMRC's SEC filing, abandoning the deal [Finding #6367].

open_questions: What compensation, if any, did GreenMet receive for brokering the Critical Metals Corp-Tanbreez partnership and the EXIM Bank letter of interest, given that no advisory agreement or fee arrangement appears in any public SEC filing?

What is the relationship between Horn's prior role creating critical minerals strategy at the Department of Energy and GreenMet's subsequent lobbying to shape the same policy area, and did any ethics obligations apply to his post-government commercial activity?

Has Ned Mamula's USGS directorship influenced any Critical Minerals List designations or policy decisions that benefit GreenMet's Greenland or other mineral projects, and is his January 2026 divestiture filing complete?

What entity currently carries GreenMet's operational activities, given that both registered DC subsidiaries (GreenMet Consulting LLC and GreenMet Real Asset Management LLC) have been withdrawn and GreenMet Technologies LLC cannot be found in any searched corporate registry?
What is the precise ownership structure of GreenMet -- specifically the equity percentages held by Horn, Sorial, Schiller, and Libra Group -- and do any undisclosed investors hold stakes?

Does the Greenland government's denial of engagement with Horn or GreenMet on the 1.5GW data center project reflect a genuine lack of contact, or diplomatic distancing amid U.S. Greenland acquisition pressure?
